description: Shakshuka is a vibrant and comforting Middle Eastern dish featuring eggs gently poached in a rich, spiced tomato and bell pepper sauce. This hearty breakfast or brunch staple is bursting with flavor, offering a perfect balance of savory, slightly sweet, and aromatic notes. It's a delightful one-pan meal that brings warmth and tradition to any table.

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics
instructions.text: Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or cast-iron pan over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and diced red bell pepper, cooking for another 5-8 minutes until the bell pepper starts to soften.

instructions.title: Build the Tomato Sauce Base
instructions.text: Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, pressing it against the bottom of the pan to deepen its flavor. Add the crushed tomatoes, ground cumin, smoked paprika, chili powder, salt, and black pepper. Stir well to combine all ingredients.

instructions.title: Simmer the Sauce
instructions.text: Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer, then reduce the heat to low. Cover the skillet and let the sauce cook for at least 15-20 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken slightly. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Prepare for Eggs
instructions.text: Once the sauce has thickened, taste and adjust seasonings as needed. Use the back of a spoon to create 4-6 small wells or indentations in the tomato sauce, spaced evenly apart.

instructions.title: Poach the Eggs
instructions.text: Carefully crack one egg into each well. Season the eggs lightly with a pinch of salt and pepper. Cover the skillet again and continue to cook on low heat for 8-12 minutes, or until the egg whites are set and the yolks are still runny to your preference.

instructions.title: Garnish and Serve
instructions.text: Remove the skillet from the heat. Garnish generously with freshly chopped parsley or cilantro. If desired, sprinkle crumbled feta cheese over the top. Serve immediately, directly from the skillet, with warm pita bread or crusty bread for dipping.

tips: For a richer flavor, allow the tomato sauce to simmer longer, letting the flavors meld beautifully; a longer simmer also thickens the sauce naturally.
Do not overcook the eggs; the yolks should remain runny for the best Shakshuka experience, perfect for dipping bread.
Serve immediately with warm pita bread, challah, or crusty bread to soak up all the delicious sauce and runny yolks.
